links.comparator_used: Accuracy across prompted reading grade levels (1-17) of LLM-simplified versions of the original radiology reports; no unsimplified-report arm
links.outcome: Clinical accuracy (radiologist assessment, PubMed-BERTScore) of LLM-simplified radiology reports by target grade level
links.effect: Accuracy stable across grades 13-11 but declined significantly below grade 11; at 7th-grade level, 20% of reports contained inaccuracies with potential to alter patient management
links.tradeoff: Inaccuracies at lower reading levels were primarily due to omission, incorrect conversion, or inappropriate generalization.
links.quote: At the 7th-grade level, 20% of reports contained inaccuracies with potential to alter patient management, primarily due to omission, incorrect conversion, or inappropriate generalization.

links.comparator_used: Different prompted target reading grade levels (1-17) within the same GPT-4 Turbo prompting approach
links.outcome: Correlation of readability scores with prompted reading level, and clinical accuracy by prompted grade level
links.effect: Readability scores correlated with prompted reading levels (r = 0.80-0.84); accuracy stable at grades 13-11 but declined significantly below grade 11; 11th grade identified as lower bound
links.tradeoff: Lower prompted grade levels reduced accuracy, with 20% of 7th-grade reports having potentially management-altering inaccuracies.
links.quote: Readability scores showed strong correlation with prompted reading levels (r = 0.80-0.84).

design_hint: reading-level constraint on LLM-simplified radiology reports
